scenes.say: Which keeps you logged in—a cookie, a session, or a token? Let's break down the basics.

scenes.label: Cookies
scenes.sub: Small data stored in your browser, often for session IDs.
scenes.say: Cookies are small pieces of data stored in your browser, often holding session IDs.

scenes.label: Sessions
scenes.sub: Session data lives on the server, linked by a session ID.
scenes.say: Sessions keep your state on the server, linked by a session ID in your cookie.

scenes.label: Tokens
scenes.sub: Tokens like JWTs are self-contained and stored client-side.
scenes.say: Tokens, like JSON Web Tokens, are self-contained and usually stored on the client.

scenes.title: Set-Cookie Example
scenes.say: Always set HttpOnly and Secure on auth cookies. SameSite adds protection against cross-site attacks.
Sessions are secure but harder to scale. Tokens scale well, but revoking them is tougher.

scenes.question: Are JWTs always more secure than sessions?
scenes.right: No—security depends on use and handling, not just the method.
scenes.say: Don't assume JWTs are always safer. Security depends on how you use and protect them.
